newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Niger seeks EU aid for parliamentary elections.
newsitem.headline: Niger seeks EU aid for parliamentary elections.

text.p: Niger has requested European Union aid in organising next month's parliamentary elections and welcomes international monitors, Niger's minister of cooperation said on Wednesday.
"We want the maximum number of observers," Ibrahim Mayaki said, adding the EU's executive commission was ready to help.

Speaking to the press after talks with the commission, Mayaki said he was on a European tour, which will also include Germany, Denmark and France, to explain the efforts of President Ibrahim Mainassara to hold open elections on November 23.
Free and fair elections would help to unblock EU financial aid to the poor West African country, suspended after General Mainassara seized power in January.
Mainassara said he acted to end a 16-month deadlock between the elected president and the prime minister that was paralysing the government of the poor West African country.
The EU was also critical after Mainassara replaced an independent electoral commission part-way through presidential elections in July. A handpicked body then declared him elected.
"The aid embargo creates economic and political pressure and threatens the future of the country," Mayaki said, adding it also made it more difficult to organise peaceful elections.
The elections have already been twice postponed and the government, which wants all opposition parties to participate, was still trying to reach agreement on procedures, Mayaki said.
